quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Which statement is true about railroad crossings?

options.text: You should use cruise control at a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to stop.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to stop.
questions.explanation: Always stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Be careful when driving near railroad tracks.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Carefully drive around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: When a school bus stops ahead on your side with red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, it is loading or unloading students. Do not proceed until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Speed up.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to safely complete the turn.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off weather conditions and reduce visibility.

questions.question: What information do blue traffic signs provide?

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance.
Distance information to specific locations.

questions.explanation: Blue signs show motorist services. They tell you about rest areas, food, hospitals, and other services nearby.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Sharp left and right turns ahead.
Winding road ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of an upcoming winding road. Adjust your speed accordingly.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you drive better.
Make you feel better.
Impair your judgment.

questions.explanation: Lack of sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment.

questions.question: As daylight fades, what should you use so others can see you?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades to help others see you. Only use high beams in open areas with no other drivers.

questions.question: What is the best way to change from one lane to another?

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Only change lanes when you need to. Every lane change increases your risk of having an accident.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, what should you do?

options.text: Still wear your seat belt.
You do not need to wear a seat belt.
Wear your seat belt behind your back.

questions.explanation: Airbags protect you in a crash. For the best protection, use your lap and shoulder belts along with the airbags.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all cars already inside the roundabout.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving a distraction?

options.text: It makes you worry about the cost of the call.
It takes up your hands, eyes, and mind.
It gets the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes up your hands, eyes, and mind.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it uses your eyes, hands, and mind. Even good drivers increase their risk of crashing when using a cell phone.

questions.question: What is a distraction while driving?

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve or avoid something.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause accidents, injuries, and death.

questions.question: You see a school bus stopped with flashing lights and the signal arm extended. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Go slowly at 15 mph if no children are visible.
Go at normal speed and watch for children.

questions.explanation: When you see a school bus stopped with flashing lights and the arm extended, you must stop completely and stay stopped until the arm goes in and the bus moves. This rule applies whether you are going the same direction as the bus or coming from the other direction.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, look to your:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look both left and right for cars and pedestrians. Look left a second time because cars from your left will be closer. Look across the whole intersection before moving to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. When you see a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop. Do not go until it is safe for you to pass through the intersection.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when can you return to your original lane?

options.text: Beep your horn.
When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, look for both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror. Only then is it safe to return to your original lane.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
Cannot result in a traffic citation.
Reduces accidents by preventing being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
questions.explanation: Tailgating can lead to aggressive driving and should be avoided. Drivers can face legal penalties for unsafe driving.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, other drivers need to see it. Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic. Turn on your emergency lights to warn other drivers.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: Your tires have less grip on wet, snowy, or icy roads than on dry roads. Slow down when the road is wet or icy.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get in the car.

questions.explanation: Safety depends on what you do before driving. Before moving your vehicle, adjust your seat, adjust your mirrors, fasten your seatbelt, and secure loose items. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.
